div.div:
Sign-in ■ blue, 1–10 · Update ■ amber, A–F · Provisioning and publishing - - grey
• 4 / B: MQTT over TLS with the key's own certificate: presence requests up; Fleet commands down, responses up. 9: over the encrypted link the watch reads the challenge (“tinycrypt-presence-v1” ‖ nonce ‖ request hash) and writes its signature.
• E: an update waits 60 s for approval through steps 3–9 (“Install tinycrypt x.y.z?”), bound to SHA-256(“tinycrypt-ota-v1” ‖ image hash ‖ version); F: write the spare slot, switch on approval, probation.
• Presence is button OR watch; the button always works on its own. The push carries no authority: approval needs the watch's Secure Enclave signature over a bonded BLE link, so the watch must be in range.
• The key is the trust anchor for updates: Fleet only triggers. An image installs only if its hash, signature and version pass and you approve it (bound to the image hash and version).
• Test only: the credential keys and the IoT private key sit in flash until the ATECC608 (CRYPT-22); secure boot and flash encryption are not yet enabled.
